do_not_assume: A group name makes it schedulable.
A saved assignment was communicated.
An accepted assignment is attendance.
goal: A bounded serving group is ready for assignments at verified locations and times.
steps: Identify the intended group type and group.
Inspect existing named locations and schedules before creating anything.
Add only the missing locations or positions and schedules.
Associate them with the serving group.
Enable Group Scheduling on the group type.
Select confirmation and reminder System Communications.
Set the confirmation and reminder offsets.
Choose `Ask` or `Auto Accept`.
Configure decline-reason and cancellation-workflow behavior.
Assign a Schedule Coordinator and choose notification events.
Test one assignment through the volunteer-facing Schedule Toolbox.
Verify the resulting assignment state and communication outcome.
Confirm that the operator is inspecting the intended group and group type.
Inspect whether `Scheduling Enabled` is active on that group type.
Confirm that the required named locations or positions exist.
Confirm that the required named schedules exist and have accurate times.
Confirm that the locations and schedules are associated with the group.
Inspect the scheduler’s current group and location selections.
If all configuration appears correct, verify permissions and the installed version before changing data.
title: Recipe: Configure a serving team for scheduling

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: The intended volunteers receive a confirmation request without an uncontrolled duplicate send.
steps: Select the correct groups, locations, schedules, and week.
Review current assignment states.
Determine whether the scheduled job has already sent the request.
Preview the confirmation communication and its response links.
Send only to the bounded eligible set.
Compare eligible-recipient count with sent count.
Review warnings and errors.
Monitor pending, confirmed, declined, and unavailable states.
Route declines or cancellations according to the configured workflow.
Verify coordinator notification separately.
title: Recipe: Send and triage volunteer confirmations

do_not_assume: RSVP enables scheduling.
A nonrespondent will appear when recipients were not registered.
An acceptance proves attendance.
goal: A group occurrence can collect and display bounded accept or decline responses.
steps: Confirm that RSVP is the intended workflow rather than Group Scheduling.
Confirm that the target group exists.
Enable RSVP on the group type.
Configure the reminder communication and offset at either group-type or group level.
Create the occurrence with its date, optional schedule, and location.
Add custom response messages when needed.
Enable and select decline reasons only when the ministry will use them.
Send the RSVP request and decide whether to register all recipients.
Monitor RSVP Detail.
Record verified phone or in-person response changes when authorized.
title: Recipe: Configure an RSVP-based serving invitation

do_not_assume: Pending means absent.
Confirmed means attended.
No attendance rows means the team met with zero volunteers.
goal: The occurrence records who served or that the team did not meet, with discrepancies ready for human review.
steps: Open the correct group attendance occurrence.
Verify the date, schedule, and location.
Mark `We Did Not Meet` if that is what occurred.
Otherwise, record actual attendees.
Add only appropriate operational notes.
Compare the completed attendance list with confirmed assignments.
Investigate late changes and data-entry omissions.
Produce a bounded follow-up list of unresolved differences.
Launch follow-up only after confirming each difference’s meaning.
title: Recipe: Close out serving attendance

do_not_assume: Watching a video is sufficient.
Completion automatically grants eligibility.
Structural feature availability proves local configuration.
goal: A volunteer completes defined learning activities and reaches an explicitly reviewed operational result.
steps: Define the readiness outcome before building activities.
Choose the appropriate program mode: on-demand or academic-calendar based.
Place the training in the relevant program, course, and class structure.
Create activities for the required learner actions.
Define completion, ordering, scoring, file, and facilitator-review expectations.
Assign staff responsibility for manual review.
Define any group sync or workflow action that should follow completion.
Test with a staff participant first.
Verify the completion record and downstream operational result independently.
Train the staff who will support volunteers.
Roll out to a bounded volunteer cohort.
Monitor exceptions before scaling.
title: Recipe: Build an LMS-based volunteer training path

do_not_assume: Do not treat generated guidance as live-instance proof.
goal: Leaders at the intended regional level receive attendance summaries for their child attendance groups.
steps: Confirm that the group hierarchy has all three required levels.
Identify the single top parent group.
Identify the region or area groups.
Confirm that intended recipients have a role marked `Is Leader` in those groups.
Confirm the child attendance groups where attendance is recorded.
Configure the Send Group Attendance Digest job for the top parent.
Run a bounded test.
Verify each recipient and the child groups represented.
Confirm the attendance-group leader link routes to the intended person.
title: Recipe: Configure an attendance digest

do_not_assume: Rock authorization grants a provider license.
A provider license grants Rock-page access.
A successful administrator test proves ordinary-user access.
goal: The Rock page and external reporting provider both authorize only the intended viewers.
steps: Identify the Rock page and report block.
Inspect Rock page and block authorization.
Define the intended security roles.
Verify the external reporting product’s licensing and identity requirements.
Test with an authorized user.
Test with an unauthorized user.
Confirm that direct report access cannot bypass the intended controls.
Review the displayed volunteer and financial fields for minimum necessary exposure.
title: Recipe: Secure an embedded volunteer dashboard

do_not_assume: Previewed v19 behavior exists in every mobile deployment.
A successful job run proves push delivery.
A scheduled touchpoint is a completed action.
Do not infer a completed follow-up from a scheduled or attempted notification.
goal: A bounded group of signed-in mobile users can see, receive, complete, and review configured outreach touchpoints.
steps: Confirm the target Rock server and mobile-shell versions.
Verify signed-in access and page placement.
Review block settings and contact-data permissions.
Configure assignment days and reminder preferences for test users.
Inspect the reminder job and time-of-day configuration.
Create bounded prayer and connection cadences.
Test dashboard visibility.
Test push delivery in the real target mobile environment.
Complete a touchpoint and verify history and pulse behavior.
Review who can see the resulting contact data before expanding access.
Confirm that the environment supports the documented v19 Rock Mobile experience.
Confirm that the person is signed in.
Inspect page placement, block settings, and authentication.
Confirm the person’s assignment days and reminder preferences.
Inspect the job’s configured time and recent execution.
Test push-notification delivery in the target mobile environment.
Inspect permissions for contact and touchpoint data.
Do not infer a completed follow-up from a scheduled or attempted notification.
title: Recipe: Pilot Outreach Toolbox for relationship-care follow-up
